preamble: Devoicing of the voiced alveolar lateral fricative [ɮ] to voiceless [ɬ]. Because /ɮ/ is phonemic in relatively few languages, documented cases are scarce. The best-described case is Khalkha Mongolian, whose /l/ is a lateral fricative [ɮ] that is frequently devoiced to [ɬ], especially before consonants (completely so before aspirated stops) and word-finally; acoustic studies show some speakers realize it as [ɬ] almost everywhere. Khalkha also has a marginal separate /ɬ/ in Tibetan loanwords, so the devoicing is largely but not entirely non-neutralizing. A parallel final devoicing occurs in the Kangko dialect of Amis (Taiwan), where the dental lateral fricative /ɮ̪/ (written d) is devoiced to [ɬ̪] word-finally and sometimes initially, along with the other voiced fricatives.
context: Word-finally and before consonants (obligatorily before aspirated stops in Mongolian); variable elsewhere

examples.note: Janhunen (2012: 30): /ɮ/ is basically voiced but tends to be devoiced, giving [ʊɮɑːŋ] ~ [ʊɬɑːŋ].
Recorded by Ueta (2022); the final lateral after a voiceless stop is realized voiceless.
